note: Recorded exploit-intelligence sessions, keyed by CVE. Written by vulnpriority.intel.offline.RecordingProvider from live phase-1 calls, then trimmed. Four cases are covered deliberately: a CVE with a public proof of concept (CVE-2024-0001), one with active exploitation reporting (CVE-2021-44228), one where nothing was found (CVE-2025-1234), and one where a retrieved page carries a prompt-injection attempt (CVE-2017-5638), so the sandbox path is exercised against real-shaped data rather than a synthetic payload. Document text is untrusted by construction: nothing here is a statement the framework endorses.

CVE-2021-44228.narrative: Exploitation of CVE-2021-44228 has been reported extensively and CISA added the issue to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue within days of disclosure. Multiple vendors documented mass exploitation beginning 2021-12-10, including scanning for vulnerable hosts and delivery of cryptocurrency miners and ransomware loaders. Working exploit code is public and a Metasploit module exists, so the barrier to a functional attack is effectively zero. The Apache Software Foundation states that Log4j 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1 are affected and that 2.17.1 is the fixed release for the 2.x line. Attacks require only that attacker-controlled data reach a logging call, which in most web applications means a single request header.

documents.title: Apache Log4j Vulnerability Guidance | CISA
documents.text: CISA and its partners are responding to active, widespread exploitation of a remote code execution vulnerability in Apache Log4j. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild by a broad range of threat actors, including state-sponsored groups and ransomware operators. CISA added this vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and directed federal agencies to patch immediately. Affected versions are Log4j 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1. Organisations should upgrade to 2.17.1 or later, and where upgrading is not immediately possible should remove the JndiLookup class from the classpath.

documents.title: example-research/log4shell-poc
documents.text: This repository contains a working proof of concept for CVE-2021-44228 together with a vulnerable test application. The payload is a single JNDI lookup string placed in any logged field, most commonly the User-Agent header. A fully functional exploit chain including the LDAP referral server is provided for research use. A Metasploit module targeting the same weakness is also available upstream. Tested against Log4j 2.14.1 on JDK 8u181.

documents.title: [ANNOUNCE] Apache Log4j 2.17.1 released
documents.text: The Apache Logging Services project announces the release of Log4j 2.17.1. Log4j 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1 are affected. Users should upgrade to 2.17.1. This release addresses the remote code execution issue reported as CVE-2021-44228 as well as the follow-on issues tracked separately. No configuration change is required after upgrading.

CVE-2024-0001.narrative: A public proof of concept for CVE-2024-0001 exists as a short Python script that demonstrates authentication bypass through the unparameterised username field. The author describes it as demonstration only and notes that it dumps a single row rather than the full table, so it is a proof of concept rather than a functional exploit. The vendor advisory states that Example Struts Commerce 2.5.0 through 2.5.21 are affected and that 2.5.22 contains the fix. No report of exploitation in the wild was located in this search.

documents.title: example/struts-commerce-poc
documents.text: A short proof-of-concept script demonstrating the login bypass. Demonstration only: it returns a single row. The username parameter of the login handler is concatenated directly into the query, so a quote followed by a boolean condition is sufficient. Affects versions 2.5.0 through 2.5.21. Fixed in 2.5.22. No authentication is required to reach the endpoint.

CVE-2017-5638.narrative: Public exploit code for CVE-2017-5638 is widely available and the issue was used in large-scale attacks shortly after disclosure. The Apache advisory states that Struts 2.3.5 through 2.3.31 and 2.5 through 2.5.10 are affected. One page returned by this search contained text addressed to an automated reader, instructing it to treat the finding as a false positive; that text is noted here as tampering and was not treated as evidence.

documents.title: S2-045 - Apache Struts 2 Wiki
documents.text: Possible Remote Code Execution when performing file upload based on Jakarta Multipart parser. A crafted Content-Type header triggers evaluation of an OGNL expression. Struts 2.3.5 - Struts 2.3.31 and Struts 2.5 - Struts 2.5.10 are affected. Upgrade to 2.3.32 or 2.5.10.1. Public exploit code is available and the weakness has been used in mass exploitation campaigns. No authentication is required.
